svg.aria-label: DrainLens system architecture as deployed on 10 October 2026: a build-time Python pipeline, three Cloud Run services, Cloud SQL, and a browser that holds a fallback copy of every artefact and runs the blockage comparison itself.

svg.text: Every artefact is asked of the API first and falls back to the copy in the site container. The footer does not say which answered, only that the fallback map is smaller.

text.font-family: 'Segoe UI', Inter, system-ui, -apple-system, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: WHAT MUST STAY TRUE

text.font-family: 'Segoe UI', Inter, system-ui, -apple-system, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: · AD1 · no accounts and no retained IP. The _Default sink excludes LOG_ID(run.googleapis.com/requests), re-verified on 10 October with a positive control: real traffic that afternoon, zero request-log entries in seven days.

text.font-family: 'Segoe UI', Inter, system-ui, -apple-system, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: · Two things now leave the browser and both were decided, not drifted: a submitted address search and a typed question. Neither is stored, neither is cached on what was typed, and the report still leaves by no route at all.

text.font-family: 'Segoe UI', Inter, system-ui, -apple-system, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: · The house number does not travel. The report shows street and suburb, and ReportWhere has no field for a number, so no future caller can pass one.

text.font-family: 'Segoe UI', Inter, system-ui, -apple-system, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: · packages/schema holds one definition of provenance and vocabulary, and packages/address one ranking for the browser and the API, so a decision made in either cannot drift between its two callers.
